sage.note: compute-engine's Ceil is Listable and threads over the list; Sage's takes scalars only.
sympy.note: compute-engine's Ceil threads over (or pools) the list; SymPy's takes scalars.

rust.note: compute-engine's Ceil is Listable and threads over the list; the Rust crates take scalars.

Rounds the real and imaginary parts up separately
sage.note: compute-engine evaluates Ceil on a complex float, rounding the real and imaginary parts up; Sage's ceil() leaves the complex argument unevaluated, printing it back symbolically.

caption: How many 5-seat vans are needed to carry 17 people
Ten bits are enough to number 1000 items, $\lceil \log_2 1000 \rceil$
$\lceil x \rceil = \lfloor x \rfloor + 1$ for non-integer x. See [[Floor]]
Floor and Ceil agree exactly on integers
A division by zero inside Ceil simplifies to ComplexInfinity
sage.note: Both decline: compute-engine answers Ceil(ComplexInfinity), and Sage's exact rational division raises a ZeroDivisionError before Ceil is even applied.
rust.note: Both decline: compute-engine answers "ComplexInfinity", and Rust's exact division panics on the zero denominator before Ceil is even applied.

caption: Rounds toward $+\infty$, not toward 0: ceil(-3.7) is -3, not -4
NaN propagates rather than erroring
wolfram.note: Both decline: compute-engine's NaN is the float can't-decide spelling (CE 0.141); Wolfram has no NaN and answers Indeterminate for the same input.
